desc: Ideation: p = A*B*C; greedy earliest-B-then-earliest-C per A occurrence is optimal; verified on Examples 1 and 4 by hand.
Implement KMP (prefix function + search) returning all start indices of a literal in s; handle the empty-literal case by treating every position 0..n as an occurrence.
Parse p into parts A, B, C by splitting on the two '*'.
Build next-occurrence arrays nextB[x] = smallest start index ≥ x where B occurs (or sentinel), and nextC[x] similarly, via reverse scans over positions 0..n.
For each occurrence i of A, compute b = nextB[i+len(A)], then c = nextC[b+len(B)]; if both valid, candidate = c + len(C) − i; track minimum.
Verify all four examples plus edge cases (p="**" → 0, empty parts, boundary matches, no-match, literal longer than s) and confirm complexity O(n + m) / O(n); deliver final code in starter format.
